messages.subject: Combining ggplots with gridExtra
parts:
Hi,

I've been trying to create a plot that combines several facetted ggplots, and a single legend. I used the approach from the gridExtra documentation (suggested in this recent post) where the legend is extracted from one of the plots then passed explicitly into the grid.arrange. I'm facing two main problems that I hope someone will be able to help me with:

1) The legend takes up a disproportionately large area, causing all the other plot components to become squashed.

2) I'm using facet_wrap with fixed scales, however the breaks and axis ticks for the x-axes are totally squashed. I'm overplotting an additional set of points from a different data source and its as if the axis calculations aren't taking the range of these values into account.

Ultimately, this will get embedded in a knitr document and rendered out using the tikzDevice, so I'm trying to make the best use of space on the page.

I've created a working example of my plot, but the data is a bit large to post inline, so I've attached the whole .R file. Here's just the plotting / data manipulation sections.

Thanks,
A 

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra) 
library(reshape) 
library(stringr) 

creme <- "#ffffb3"
pale.purple <- "#bebada" 
olive.green <- "#b2df8a" 
darker.blue <- "#1f77b4" 
light.yellow <- "#ffff99" 
my.colours <- c(olive.green, darker.blue, light.yellow, creme, pale.purple) 

hard.constraints <- c("event.clashes","overlaps","room.valid")
soft.constraints <- c("final.timeslot","three.in.a.row","single.event") 

ids <- c("instance", "partition", "search", "delta", "run.no", "scope", "preserve", "id", "nhoods", "config")

nhood.symbols <- c(15:18, 7)
nhood.scale <- scale_shape_manual(name = "Neighbourhood Set", values = nhood.symbols) 

jitter <- position_jitter(width=0, height = 0.1)

base_size <- theme_bw()$text$size
grid_title_par <- gpar(fontsize=(base_size * 1.2)) 

mySortByInstance <- function(data) {

# assume data$instance is of form <type><number>, perhaps
# with underscore between. Sort by type, breaking ties
# with number.

id <- as.numeric(str_extract(data$instance, "\\d{1,}quot;))
type <- factor(str_extract(data$instance, "^[[:alpha:]]+"), levels=c("competition", "small", "med", "big"))

return(data[order(type, id, decreasing = TRUE), , drop=TRUE])
}

makePlot <- function(data, starts, plot.func = createComparisonPlot, title = NULL, constraints = c(hard.constraints, soft.constraints), display.y = TRUE, LaTeX.labels = FALSE, legend = FALSE){

starts <- mySortByInstance(subset(starts, variable %in% constraints))
data <- mySortByInstance(subset(data, variable %in% constraints))

order(data$instance)

theme_update(plot.title=element_text(size = base_size))
plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = value, y = instance))
plot <- plot + geom_point(aes(colour = search, shape = nhoods), alpha=I(0.5), position = jitter) + scale_colour_manual(name = "Bypass Neighbourhoods", values = my.colours, labels=c("No","Yes"))

plot <- plot + facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "fixed", ncol = 1)

plot <- plot + geom_point(data = starts, colour = "red", shape = 4, size = 3)
plot <- plot + nhood.scale

plot <- plot + theme_bw() + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank())

if(!display.y){
plot <- plot + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())  
}


if(legend){

plot <- plot + theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", legend.direction = "horizontal", legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white"), legend.background = element_rect(fill="lightBlue"), legend.margin = unit(c(0,0,0,0), "lines"), plot.margin = unit(c(0,1,0,0), "lines")) + guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(alpha = 1)))

} else {
plot <- plot + theme(legend.position = "none", plot.margin = unit(c(0,1,0,0), "lines"))
}

plot <- plot + ggtitle(title)

}

createFullPlot <- function(data, starts, plot.func=createComparisonPlot, instances = data$instance, title = NULL){
starts.data <- subset(starts, instance %in% instances)
starts.data$instance <- droplevels(starts.data$instance)
m.starts <- melt(starts.data, id.vars = c("instance"))

subset.data <- subset(data, instance %in% instances)
subset.data$instance <- droplevels(subset.data$instance)
m.data <- melt(subset.data, id.vars = ids)
m.data$partition <- droplevels(m.data$partition)

hard.plots <- lapply(levels(m.data$partition), function(x){ is.left.plot <- (x == levels(m.data$partition)[1]); makePlot(subset(m.data, partition == x), m.starts, plot.func, x, constraints = hard.constraints, display.y = is.left.plot, legend = is.left.plot) })

soft.plots <- lapply(levels(m.data$partition), function(x){ makePlot(subset(m.data, partition == x), m.starts, plot.func, constraints = soft.constraints, display.y = (x == levels(m.data$partition)[1])) })

total.plots <- lapply(levels(m.data$partition), function(x){ makePlot(subset(m.data, partition == x), m.starts, plot.func, constraints = "total", display.y = (x == levels(m.data$partition)[1])) } )

# Extract the legend from the top plot.

tmp <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(hard.plots[[1]]))
leg <- which(sapply(tmp$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box") 
legend <- tmp$grobs[[leg]]
hard.plots[[1]] <- hard.plots[[1]] + theme(legend.position = "none")

plot.list <- c(hard.plots, soft.plots, total.plots) 
no.of.cols <- ceiling(length(plot.list) / 3) 
args.list <- c(plot.list, list(nrow=length(plot.list), ncol=length(levels(m.data$partition)))) 

grid.arrange(legend, do.call(arrangeGrob, args.list), clip = FALSE, ncol=1, main = textGrob(title, gp=grid_title_par), left = "Problem Instance")

}

createPlots <- function(data.set, master.func=createFullPlot, instances = NULL, title=NULL){ 
func.args <- list(data.set, starts, instances = instances, title = title)
do.call(master.func, func.args)
}

convertNames <- function(x) {

s <- unlist(strsplit(x, "\\."))
d <- lapply(s[-1], function(x) { paste(toupper(substring(x, 1,1)), substring(x, 2), sep="", collapse="") } )
return(paste(s[1], paste(d, collapse=""), sep=""))
}

first.comp <- list(instances = c(paste("competition0", 1:3, sep="")))
vns.args <- list(data.set, title = "Effect of Bypassing Redundant Neighbourhoods") 
do.call(createPlots, c(vns.args, first.comp))
